disease.category: Metabolic / Inborn Error of Purine Metabolism
disease.mechanism: Loss-of-function. Deficiency of HPRT1 (hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase) blocks the purine salvage pathway, causing massive de novo purine synthesis and uric acid overproduction. This leads to hyperuricemia (kidney stones, gout, tophi) plus a poorly-understood neurological syndrome: severe motor dysfunction, intellectual disability, and characteristic self-injurious behaviour (SIB).
disease.autotac_rationale: NOT eligible. LNS is a loss-of-function enzyme deficiency — HPRT is missing, not accumulated. Degrading any residual HPRT would worsen the disease. Correct routes are enzyme replacement / gene therapy / urate-lowering (allopurinol), not protein degradation.
disease.prevalence: ~1 in 380,000 (commonly cited; X-linked, almost exclusively males) — UNVERIFIED exact figure this session
disease.age_of_onset: Infancy (developmental delay); self-injury typically from age 2-3

approved_treatments.mechanism_correct: Lowers uric acid production by inhibiting xanthine oxidase. It treats the hyperuricemia (kidney stones, gout, tophi) but does NOT improve the neurological or behavioural symptoms.
approved_treatments.note: Standard urate-lowering therapy for LNS. Addresses the metabolic consequence, not the neurological phenotype.

disease.human_summary: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is an X-linked disorder of purine metabolism caused by complete HPRT1 deficiency. Affected boys develop uric acid overproduction (kidney stones, gout) alongside severe neurological disability and a striking, near-universal self-injurious biting behaviour. Allopurinol controls the uric acid but not the neurology.
